subject: Science

sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: Earth, Moon, and the Sun 12 , , the Sun 12 One morning in Kanniyakumari, Tamil Nadu, 12-year-old Rashmika was eagerly cycling to school.
sections.source_evidence: Earth, Moon, and the Sun 12 , , the Sun 12 One morning in Kanniyakumari, Tamil Nadu, 12-year-old Rashmika was eagerly cycling to school.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: That was the day her science teacher had dedicated a class for students to share and try to explain interesting observations.
sections.source_evidence: That was the day her science teacher had dedicated a class for students to share and try to explain interesting observations.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: Rashmika had been noticing that the coconut tree shadows were long in the morning but shorter in the afternoon on her way back.
sections.source_evidence: Rashmika had been noticing that the coconut tree shadows were long in the morning but shorter in the afternoon on her way back.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: She thought about it and decided that the size of the shadows changed because the Sun moved across the sky during the day.
sections.source_evidence: She thought about it and decided that the size of the shadows changed because the Sun moved across the sky during the day.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: But she also remembered learning that the Earth moved around the Sun (in chapter ‘Beyond Earth’ in the Grade 6 Science textbook Curiosity) so she was puzzled.
sections.source_evidence: But she also remembered learning that the Earth moved around the Sun (in chapter ‘Beyond Earth’ in the Grade 6 Science textbook Curiosity) so she was puzzled.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: She wondered — does the Sun move in the sky?
sections.source_evidence: She wondered — does the Sun move in the sky?

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: Curiosity Textbook of Science Grade 7 170 12.1 Rotation of the Earth You might have also noticed that the Sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
